title: Liverpool sell Bobby Duncan to Fiorentina amid ‘bullying’ claim
trail: Liverpool have accepted an improved offer from Fiorentina for Bobby Duncan days after the striker’s agent accused the club of ‘mentally bullying’ the teenager
body: Liverpool have accepted an improved offer from Fiorentina for Bobby Duncan days after the striker’s agent accused the club of “mentally bullying” the teenager. The 18-year-old has signed a three-year contract with the Italian club, who have agreed a £1.8m fee plus 20% of any sell-on with Liverpool. Last week Liverpool rejected Fiorentina’s offer to take Duncan, who is a cousin of Steven Gerrard, on loan with a view to a £1.5m summer transfer, prompting a furious statement from the player’s agent, Saif Rubie, that mired Duncan in controversy. On Friday Jürgen Klopp suggested a contract dispute was at the heart of Duncan’s standoff with his boyhood club and hoped a resolution could be found. Fiorentina’s latest bid, however, will give Liverpool a healthy return on an academy prospect they signed for £200,000 from Manchester City last year. The profit available, combined with the unseemly episode over the player’s future, prompted Liverpool’s decision to part company with Duncan, who scored 32 goals for their youth teams last season. He was also involved in a contract dispute with City, when under a different agent and believed he should have been part of Liverpool’s senior squad rather than playing for the under‑18s and under-23s. Duncan missed the under‑23s game at Southampton last week because of stress, his agent said. Liverpool dismissed Rubie’s allegations against the club and the sporting director, Michael Edwards, as unfounded and inaccurate. The Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk has been shortlisted for the Fifa men’s player of the year award. He is up against Barcelona’s Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo of Juventus, having beaten the illustrious pair to Uefa’s player of the year award last week. Klopp has been shortlisted in the men’s manager category with Tottenham’s Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester City’s Pep Guardiola.
